title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 392, page 4-38) of Commutative Algebra, Chapter VII 'Diviseurs', §4, filed among Grothendieck's handwritten L-function notes. The neighbouring pages are handwritten computations on the functional equation of L-functions.

The mathematics, in modern terms:

(1) End of the proof of formula (23). The setting is a finite extension A ⊂ B of noetherian integrally closed domains, with B finitely generated as an A-module. Formula (23) says that for a finitely generated A-module M, the divisor class of the base change satisfies c_B(M⊗_A B) = i(c_A(M)). Here:
- c denotes the class in the divisor class group C(·);
- χ denotes the 'characteristic' (content) divisor of a torsion module;
- i : C(A) → C(B) is the pullback of divisor classes.
The argument uses Q, which differs from M by a pseudo-null module, the additivity results of n°7 Prop. 16, and statement (ii), the compatibility of χ with base change.

(2) Remark 1. Reflexivity is not preserved by base change in general, but it is preserved when B is flat over A.

(3) Remark 2. For a tower A ⊂ B ⊂ C, the norms and pullbacks are transitive: N_{C/A} = N_{B/A}∘N_{C/B} and i_{C/A} = i_{C/B}∘i_{B/A}. This follows from the multiplicativity of ramification indices and residue degrees.

(4) Start of n°9 'Un théorème de réduction', with Lemma 6, a prime-avoidance-type lemma. Let p_1, …, p_n be distinct primes of R, and let H_i ⊂ R/p_i be subsets such that no translate α_i + H_i contains a nonzero ideal of R/p_i. Then some a ∈ R has its image in each R/p_i outside H_i. Part (ii) says the hypothesis holds whenever Card H_i < Card(R/p_i).

In the published Bourbaki AC VII §4 n°9, I believe this lemma serves the reduction theorem: a finitely generated torsion-free module M over a noetherian integrally closed domain has a free submodule L with M/L isomorphic to an ideal. I am not certain of the exact published numbering.

The proof begins by induction on n, after reordering so that p_1 is extremal (presumably minimal or maximal) among the p_i. The page breaks off here.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. Part (ii) is correct: a nonzero ideal xD of a domain D is in bijection with D, so it has cardinality Card(D) and cannot fit inside a translate of a smaller set.
The exercise reference in Remark 1 is left blank ('exerc.   '), which is typical of a draft.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft of AC VII §4 (divisors), which was published essentially in this form in 1965. It is not original Grothendieck material, and its link to the surrounding L-function notes is only archival.
transcription_corrections: The symbol written χ is a script/gothic chi (the characteristic divisor of a torsion module), typed by hand-overstrike.
'(exerc.  )' contains a blank where the exercise number was meant to go.
